summary: Beijing blocks SoftBank's purchase of ABB's robot business in China, shoppers ask strangers to veto their carts before Double 11, and Starbucks China ends free seating.
body: China's foreign-investment security review office has prohibited SoftBank's purchase of ABB's robotics business in China, ABB said on Nov 5.[^1] SoftBank agreed in 2025 to buy the whole ABB Robotics division for about US$5.4 billion, and China is the unit's largest market.[^1][^2] No official reason was given; reports point to Beijing wanting to keep factory know-how and data at home, which has not been confirmed.[^2][^3] ABB says the two companies are still working on the deal.[^1] My read: as robots become central to China's factories, Beijing is treating them like chips, as strategic technology.

Before Double 11 (Nov 11), China's biggest online sale, apps where friends or strangers vote on whether you should buy what is in your cart have spread, Sixth Tone reports.[^4] One, "Still Want to Buy?", passed 500,000 users within weeks; over 85% were women under 24.[^4] Platforms are reshaping the sale for careful shoppers, with simpler flat discounts instead of complicated coupons, and last year's sales grew about half as fast as the year before.[^5]

Daily life: Starbucks China now requires customers to buy something before sitting down, ending its open-seating habit at about 8,000 mainland cafés.[^6] China Mobile, the state phone company, plans to spend more than 100 billion yuan (about US$15 billion) on computing for AI in 2027.[^7] China's October trade figures are due Nov 10.
differences: ABB's statement says only the China part of the deal is prohibited, while many headlines say the whole deal was blocked; whether it can be restructured without China is unclear.[^1][^2]
